state_of_the_art.statement: The maximum is 86 = floor(256/3) + 1, attained by {171, ..., 256}. An exact integer programme (151,333 divisibility constraints, solved to optimality with HiGHS; scripts/check_state_of_the_art.py --slow) shows that no larger subset of [1,256] has the property. Bedert proved the bound floor(n/3) + 1 for all sufficiently large n, as conjectured by Erdős and Sárközy.
